description: Table 2, a text-only table rendered as an image (no plots, micrographs or schematics), titled "Elastic moduli calculated from different ranges". It has four columns: "Species", "Conditions", and a spanning header "Elastic modulus at region of strain (%)" subdivided into "0–0.05" and "Whole elastic range". Five species rows are listed: A, "As received" → 182 (0–0.05 % strain) and 173 (whole elastic range); B, "With 15% pre-strain" → 188 and 162; C, "Heat-treated after 15% pre-strain" → 186 and 162; D, "Heat-treated after received" → 189 and 189; E, "Annealed" → 224 and 206. No units for the elastic modulus are printed anywhere on the table; no error bars, uncertainty or statistical columns appear. The table demonstrates that the modulus measured over the narrow initial strain window (0–0.05 %) always exceeds that measured over the whole elastic range, and that the gap between the two is small only for D (189 vs 189) and E (224 vs 206), while B and C show the largest discrepancy (188/186 vs 162/162); the annealed species E has the highest modulus in both columns.
measured_quantities: elastic modulus at 0–0.05 % strain region (unit not printed on the table)
elastic modulus over the whole elastic range (unit not printed on the table)

observations.observation: The table lists five species rows labelled A–E, with conditions 'As received', 'With 15% pre-strain', 'Heat-treated after 15% pre-strain', 'Heat-treated after received' and 'Annealed'.
The two elastic-modulus columns are headed 'Elastic modulus at region of strain (%)' with sub-headings '0–0.05' and 'Whole elastic range'.
Printed values are: A 182 and 173; B 188 and 162; C 186 and 162; D 189 and 189; E 224 and 206.
For every species the modulus from the 0–0.05 % strain window is greater than or equal to the modulus from the whole elastic range.
Species E (Annealed) has the highest values in both columns (224 and 206), exceeding all other species.
Species D (Heat-treated after received) is the only row where the two moduli are equal (189 and 189).
Species B and C share the same whole-elastic-range value (162) despite different conditions (15% pre-strain versus heat-treated after 15% pre-strain).
No unit for the elastic modulus (e.g. GPa) is printed on the table.
The caption states the table gives elastic moduli calculated from different ranges.

The citing text states the elastic moduli were calculated from the initial stage (strain < 0.1%) and from the whole elastic region, whereas the table column header reads 0–0.05; the two strain-window descriptions disagree.

The citing text asserts that the elastic modulus remains almost the same until yielding only for the annealed workpiece, consistent with the near-equal D row and the small E-row difference in the table.

The citing text explains the behaviour as recovery of the Cottrell effect, with heat treatment restraining movable dislocations, and states that piled-up dislocations from plastic deformation cause a decrease of the apparent elastic modulus.
